### D3YXK2 — Scaffold attachment factor B1

entities.name: SAFB1
observations: The 768-aa query sequence matches reviewed mouse SAFB1 (UniProt D3YXK2) at 100% identity and 100% query coverage; the reference protein is 937 aa and the query appears to represent a shorter isoform or partial form.
SAFB1 is a nuclear scaffold/matrix attachment region DNA-binding protein that organizes transcription and RNA-processing complexes.
SAFB1 contains an N-terminal SAP domain and a central RNA-recognition motif (RRM), supported by Pfam matches at residues 31–66 and 431–499 of the query.
SAFB1 is predicted to be highly acidic, hydrophilic, intrinsically disordered, and low-complexity-rich: pI 4.88, charge at pH 7 approximately −49, GRAVY −1.23, instability index 71.75.

The protein has extensive acidic and serine-rich regions, basic nuclear-localization sequences, and a basic helical/coiled-coil-like C-terminal region, consistent with regulated nuclear protein interactions.

Curated homolog annotations support chromatin/S-MAR DNA binding, RNA binding, transcriptional regulation, mRNA-processing regulation, estrogen-receptor corepressor activity, and interactions with RNA polymerase II and splicing factors.
No catalytic activity, enzyme motif, transmembrane segment, or signal peptide is supported by the available analysis.

entities.name: SAFB1 nuclear scaffold function
observations: Reviewed mammalian SAFB1 annotations describe a nuclear scaffold protein that binds S/MAR DNA and couples transcription with RNA processing through interactions with RNA polymerase II and SR-family splicing proteins.
SAFB1 can act as an estrogen-receptor corepressor and, in specific complexes, regulate transcription positively or negatively depending on partner context.
